answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The beacon multiplier is published, charged in dune, and quartz lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1244 identities would post 4717 proofs and burn roughly 66 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
